metaDescription: Picture Rocks, Lycoming County mineral rights owner along the Loyalsock? We buy oil and gas interests, explain the courthouse paperwork, fair cash offers.
heroLead: Picture Rocks sits along the Loyalsock Creek in Lycoming County, timber and farm country that saw real Marcellus leasing activity during the boom years, and mineral tracts here often trace back to family land that's been worked for generations.
intro: We understand the pull of holding onto land your family has farmed or timbered for generations, and selling mineral rights doesn't mean giving that up — it just separates what's under the ground from what's on top of it. For Picture Rocks families sitting on a fractional interest that's been more confusing than valuable, that separation can be a relief.

sections.heading: Lycoming County's Marcellus Timeline
paragraphs: Leasing activity picked up here later than it did in the earliest Susquehanna and Bradford County boom years, so a number of Picture Rocks leases were signed with somewhat better terms as landowners in the region learned from what happened further north. Even so, post-production deductions remain a common source of frustration, and we'll go through your statement with you if you're not sure whether the numbers look right.
Loyalsock-area tracts vary in value depending on unit participation, so we check recorded spacing units against your parcel before quoting anything specific.

sections.heading: Selling Without Losing Your Land
paragraphs: A mineral rights sale only transfers the subsurface interest — your family keeps the surface, the house, the fields, everything above ground, unless you specifically choose otherwise. For a lot of Picture Rocks owners, that distinction is what makes selling minerals an easy decision even when keeping the land itself is non-negotiable.

faqs.question: If I sell my mineral rights, do I still own my land?
faqs.answer: Yes. Selling minerals only transfers the subsurface oil and gas rights, not your surface property.

faqs.question: Is my area still seeing active Marcellus drilling?
faqs.answer: We check current activity near your specific parcel, since it varies within Lycoming County, and give you an honest read on where things stand.

faqs.question: What if my lease terms seem better than what I've heard from other counties?
faqs.answer: That's possible. Leases signed later in the boom, including many in this part of Lycoming County, sometimes carried more favorable royalty language than the earliest leases up north.

faqs.question: Can you buy a timber-and-mineral tract where we've kept the timber rights separate?
faqs.answer: Yes, we buy the mineral interest alone and have no interest in your timber rights, so any existing timber arrangement your family has stays completely untouched by the sale.
